key_insight: The paper frames end-to-end entanglement fidelity as the quantum-network equivalent of QoT and studies when a controller should compute it analytically, simulate it, or learn it from data. The core takeaway is that the best choice depends on the tradeoff between accuracy, latency, and deployment conditions.
problem_solved: Quantum network controllers need fast, reliable estimates of path quality to support routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. This work addresses how to estimate transmission quality in time for control decisions without sacrificing too much accuracy.
method: Compares three estimation strategies: analytical computation, simulation, and machine learning.
Focuses on end-to-end fidelity as the central quality metric for candidate quantum paths.
Provides a decision-oriented view of which estimation method is appropriate under different operational constraints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper highlights a realistic control problem where learned models may complement or replace expensive physics-based estimation. It is useful for designing low-latency predictors in quantum networking systems where inference speed and reliability are critical.

paper_title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
paper_authors: Anis Bekri, Amar Abane, Van Sy Mai, Abdella Battou, Saddek Bensalem
